items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: It’s an album that Tito Puente did with Mongo Santamaria, Patato and some other percussionists and a bass player.

ctx.x: It’s an album that Tito Puente did with Mongo Santamaria, Patato and some other percussionists and a bass player. [Scats] Then they would solo around that. So that’s a possibility. I haven’t thought about it. You just gave me the idea.

items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I remember one time playing with, it was like top musicians, except for myself. I was the young one. It was Manny Duran who played with the Machito orchestra, Eddie Martinez who played with Chico O’Farrill, everybody Gato Barbieri, Patato on congas.

ctx.x: I remember one time playing with, it was like top musicians, except for myself. I was the young one. It was Manny Duran who played with the Machito orchestra, Eddie Martinez who played with Chico O’Farrill, everybody Gato Barbieri, Patato on congas. The bass player was Victor Menenguez a veteran from the scene. We were playing. Midway the coordinator stopped us, paid us, sent us home, they put a boom box in the middle of the room and people again just started dancing. So they didn’t even appreciate the Latino…
Let’s suppose you went to a party and someone asks you what you do and, “Well I play a lot of Latin jazz.” And that person said, “What makes Latin jazz different from jazz?”
